thread.title: Morning Movers: Dr. Pepper Soars on Keurig Merger; Seagate Technology Climbs on Earnings

author: Ben Levisohn
title: Morning Movers: Dr. Pepper Soars on Keurig Merger; Seagate Technology Climbs on Earnings
text:
Stocks look set for a lower open this morning as the 10-year Treasury yield rose to its highest level since 2014.
S&P 500 futures have declined 0.2%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures have dipped 0.2%. Nasdaq Composite futures have fallen 0.2%. The 10-year Treasury has risen 0.045 percentage point to 2.71%.
We probably should have expected some weakness this morning considering the market's big gains last week . And it's not as if there's not enough news on tap to keep markets on edge. There's the Fed meeting on Wednesday , and the U.S. payrolls report on Friday , where the pace of wage increases could determine how much higher bond yields can go.
Illustration: Bloomberg News But look to earnings to prompt the biggest market moves. Apple (AAPL), Facebook (FB), Alphabet (GOOGL), Microsoft (MSFT) and Amazon.com (AMZN) are all set to report earnings this week. Cornerstone Marco's Carter Worth notes that together these five stocks, the biggest in the S&P 500 have, have a market capitalization of $3.65 trillion and make up more than 14% of the benchmark. Of course, they could be non-events, as losses and gains could cancel each other out.
But there are two big options, Worth writes. "The market surges yet again, yet another week -in response to fantastic results from the leading stocks in the land- and spikes so hard that a much-anticipated “blow off top” is made," he explains. "Or Apple, Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Facebook somehow “disappoint” in some sort of bizarre, unanticipated, group miss, or not-good-enough beat, and the market slumps in response."
Should be fun.
Morning Movers: Dr. Pepper Snapple Group (DPS) has surged $132.64 after agreeing to merge with Keurig Green Mountain to form a new company called Keurig Dr. Pepper, Wells Fargo's Bonnie Herzog notes that Dr. Pepper shareholders will receive a special cash dividend of $103.75 a share, and own 13% of the new company, who called the announcement a "surprise."
Avon Products (AVP) has jumped 10% to $2.67 after shareholders called on the company to sell itself . "The Shareholder Group is extremely disappointed with the deteriorating operating and share price performance that has occurred under the stewardship of the current Board," the shareholders said in a press release . "The Shareholder Group is also dismayed by the Board’s failure to act quickly and decisively on the past recommendations its members have made to improve the long-term performance of the Company, including promptly hiring a new chief executive officer – a step that has been long overdue and members of the Shareholder Group recommended over two years ago."
Lockheed Martin (LMT) has gained 2.9% to $354.88 after reporting a profit of $4.30 a share on sales of $15.1 billion. Analyst had been predicting earnings of $4.07 on sales of $14.7 billion. Lockheed had gained 7.4% this year heading into today's print, and is up 36% during the past 12 months.
Seagate Technology (STX) has climbed 3.5% to $56.86 after reporting a profit of $1.48 a share on sales of $2.91 billion. Analysts had been forecasts earnings of $1.35 on sales of $2.86 billion. Seagate has gained 31% in January but has only risen 23% during the past 12 months.
Myriad Genetics (MYGN) has dropped 7.7% to $37.87 after getting initiated with a Sell rating at Goldman Sachs. Goldman sighted excessive valuation and overly optimistic sentiment regarding the possibility of reimbursement for its GeneSight product.
Wynn Resorts (WYNN) has fallen 3.9% to $180.29 today as its slide continues following allegations of sexual harassment against CEO Steve Wynn . "We think the news reports alleging sexual harassment by Steve Wynn creates a sizable overhang in the shares and see value that compensates investors for risk related to these allegations at the ~$150 level, versus the ~$180 level it last traded on Friday," JPMorgan's Joseph Greff wrote in a note over the weekend.
Gilead Earnings: The Lesson From AbbVie Gilead Sciences (GILD) isn't set to report earnings until Feb. 6, but investors got a big hint about what they might hold when AbbVie (ABBV) released its own earnings on Friday...and it wasn't good.
You wouldn't know it based on how Gilead's stock performed this past Friday--it surged 5.3% to $85.46 following a Jefferies upgrade . AbbVie, for its part, surged 14%, making it the biggest gainer in the S&P 500 .
But AbbVie's earnings contained some bad news for Gilead and its Hepatitis-C treatments, says BMO Capital Markets analyst M. Ian Somaiya. He notes that AbbVie's strong hepatitis-C guidance--they're expecting sales of $2.5 billion or more--suggests that Wall Street's predictions for Gilead's own hepatitis-C sales are likely too strong. This is coming from someone who is already more bearish on hep-C than his peers--while the consensus is for hep-C sales of $5.5 billion, Somaiya has modeled just $4.9 billion.
But Somaiya is preparing for worse. "We think the market is ready to turn the page on HCV and would view guidance of $3-4bn as a clearing event for GILD," he writes. Whether that's considered good news or bad remains to be seen.
Gilead Sciences has fallen 0.7% to $84.83 in pre-open trading this morning, while AbbVie has dropped 2% to $120.77 after getting downgraded to Market Perform from Outperform at Leerink.
The View From Silicon Valley In six days, Tom Brady will attempt to win a record sixth time in a record eighth Super Bowl.
If successful, he won’t be the only winner.
Facebook will anxiously be watching along with the rest of America. Its rooting interest, like any self-respecting media operation, is in a compelling performance from Brady, the biggest star of the country’s biggest sporting event, to spur ratings and – ultimately – revenue.
Brady is star of a new documentary series “Tom vs. Time” on the TV-like digital hangout, Facebook Watch, which is crucial to the company’s strategy. It is in sports that Facebook and several of its fiercest rivals see a path to increased traffic, advertising sales and revenue.
Facebook, Amazon and – perhaps – Twitter (TWTR) and Alphabet's YouTube are in the running for streaming rights to English Premier League soccer matches in the UK. An auction is scheduled in February.
For Facebook, which bid $600 million for the Internet broadcast rights to an Indian cricket league in 2016 and has streamed some live college football and professional baseball games, the series with Brady underscores its newfound push for “meaningful social interaction.”
“We’ve found that communities formed around video like TV shows or sports create a greater sense of belonging than many other kinds of communities,” Facebook Chief Executive Officer Mark Zuckerberg told stock analysts in November.
With changes to Facebook’s News Feed that diminish third-party videos, it could enhance audiences for Watch and Facebook Live, increasing interest in the Brady docu-series and other original programming.
As goes TB12 in Super Bowl LII on Sunday, so go the fortunes of his media partner, Facebook. -- Jon Swartz
